findings.evidence: B-04: "the enumeration is a new exported function in `src/qa-review.ts` ... and it issues its own `git` reads with `execFileSync` rather than calling into `src/git.ts`"; B-01: "**Decision recorded here:** `src/git.ts` stays outside this slice's scope ... are therefore implemented inside files this slice already owns, not by widening `src/git.ts`"; B-05: "it is a deterministic function of its `(cwd, fromRef, toRef)` arguments alone, holding no orchestrator, run-state or run-slug state"
findings.expected: With an exhaustive file-scope map and a file-scope gate shipping in the same PRD, every git operation these two behaviors newly perform must either be reachable from an already-exported src/git.ts function on declared evidence, or src/git.ts must appear in fileScope with the addition named as an in-scope behavior.
findings.observed: The revision names both seams unambiguously and takes a third route the clear-condition's concern permits: neither read touches src/git.ts at all. B-04's status read is a new exported function in src/qa-review.ts (in fileScope) called once from runQAStage, issuing `status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` plus an `--ignored` status with `-c core.quotePath=false`; B-05's read is performed in src/change-summary.ts (in fileScope). The reasons the existing exports cannot serve are verified against the tree: git.statusPorcelain (src/git.ts:489) does issue exactly `["status", "--porcelain"]` and its own docstring records that the ship gate parses its output; git.logCommitsWithStat (src/git.ts:726) is hard-wired to `${base}..HEAD`; git.listChangedFiles (src/git.ts:1272) returns a union path set; the core.quotePath rationale is at src/git.ts:1296-1305. B-01's "four helpers" claim is narrowed to the worktree lifecycle and each helper is named with a line cite; a new non-goal forbids adding, amending or widening any src/git.ts export; a Definition-of-done item requires src/git.ts to be unmodified and names both hosting files; B-04's acceptance behavior asserts "src/git.ts is unmodified" and B-05's asserts the same. B-05's purity claim is restated as argument-determinism with its git reads located, and its test-plan scenario now runs in a temp repo and asserts repeat-call stability.
findings.clearCondition: For B-04's status read and B-05's two-ref read, the contract names the seam unambiguously and either cites the existing exported src/git.ts function each one calls (including one whose output covers ignored paths under .afk/), or adds src/git.ts to fileScope and the file list with the new primitive named as an in-scope behavior and the exhaustive-map departure stated; B-05's "pure" claim is restated to say where its git reads are performed.

findings.evidence: B-08 observable: "src/prompt-template.test.ts asserts the prompt text contains the four questions, both halves of the probe rule, and the discard instruction; no spawned suite asserts the prompt text"
findings.expected: A static prompt-text obligation should be observed by the cheapest test that can see it, and the observable should cover every clause its `then` promises.
findings.observed: The observable now names all three obligations its `then` promises and lands the assertion in src/prompt-template.test.ts, which is verified to be a non-spawned suite that already readFileSyncs prompt and persona text over `new URL("../...", import.meta.url)` in the cited region. The hosting file is added both to fileScope and to "Files expected to change", the test-plan scenario says the same, and the Definition-of-done item spells out "not in a spawned suite".
findings.clearCondition: B-08's observable names the discard clause as well as the four questions and both probe-rule halves, and places the assertion in a non-spawned suite (adding the hosting test file to fileScope if none is listed) or says why the rendering path is only reachable from a spawned run.

findings.evidence: B-02 observable: "...and observes the seed manifest only through its declared consequence: no reviewer-write-violation event names contract.md or acceptance-manifest.json for that attempt"
findings.expected: Each clause of an observable result should read a surface a test can actually reach.
findings.observed: The observable no longer asserts the contents of an in-memory set with no declared surface. It keeps the amended-bytes clause and restates the second clause as the run-event consequence B-04's observable already reads, and B-02's `then` now states that consequence ("so the seeded pair is invisible to B-04's scan") so the observable covers every clause the `then` promises.
findings.clearCondition: B-02's observable either names the surface that exposes the seed manifest (an event payload, a written artifact, or an exported helper's return value) or is restated as the no-violation consequence B-04 already observes.
